answer: Quadratic admission pricing: each epoch the registry auctions identity slots like lots of timber; an agent's nth slot costs n fee units. An honest user buys one slot and pays once, while a sybil operator needing N puppets pays 1+2+...+N, about N^2/2 per round — no bulk discount, since fees burn at settlement. 100 vote-boosting replicas cost 5,050 units per round, so operator cost passes the zenith cap, the maximum weight one agent may hold, far below where vote buying pays. Expired slots decay into relic records that cannot be revived; re-entry restarts the ladder at one.
